challenges.name: The Opening
challenges.description: Get three different people to say the name of a chess opening (e.g. "Sicilian," "London," "Caro-Kann") without saying one yourself first.
challenges.hint: Someone is very curious about how other people like to start things.

challenges.name: Castling
challenges.description: Swap seats with someone at two different pubs without either of them noticing it was deliberate.
challenges.hint: Somebody's memory for where they were sitting seems suspiciously poor.

challenges.name: En Passant
challenges.description: Take something (a crisp, a drink, a chess piece) from someone's side of the table just after they've put it down, 3 times without any of them commenting on it.
challenges.hint: Keep an eye on whatever you've just put down.

challenges.name: Promotion
challenges.description: Convince someone to give you a "title" for the night, like a nickname that sticks for at least one full pub.
challenges.hint: Someone is angling for a promotion tonight.

challenges.name: The Fork
challenges.description: Get two different people to ask you the same question within five minutes.
challenges.hint: Someone wants to hear the same words from two directions.

challenges.name: Zugzwang
challenges.description: Get two different people to say "I don't know what to do" or "I'm stuck."
challenges.hint: Someone wants to leave people with no good options.

challenges.name: Checkmate
challenges.description: Use the words "check" or "mate" naturally in conversation five times each (e.g. "let me check," "cheers, mate").
challenges.hint: Listen for someone with two small words they can't stop using.

challenges.name: The Knight's Move
challenges.description: Every time you move to a new spot in a pub, go somewhere L-shaped from where you were.
challenges.hint: Watch how people get from one spot to the next.

challenges.name: Blunder
challenges.description: Deliberately get three different well-known chess facts slightly wrong without anyone correcting you.
challenges.hint: Someone's chess knowledge seems a little shakier than it should be.

challenges.name: Stalemate
challenges.description: Get into a friendly debate with 2 different people (not at the same time) that ends with you both agreeing to disagree.
challenges.hint: Someone is happy to argue but never seems to want to win.

challenges.name: Gambit
challenges.description: Give something away early in the night (a crisp, your seat, a coaster) and get something better back from the same person before the crawl ends.
challenges.hint: Someone's generosity may come with a catch later in the night.

challenges.name: Touch-Move
challenges.description: Any item of someone else's that you touch on the table, you must move to a new spot before letting go. Do this at least three times in the night.
challenges.hint: Someone can't seem to leave things exactly where they found them.

challenges.name: Resignation
challenges.description: Get two different people to say "I give up," "fine, you win," or "I resign."
challenges.hint: Someone is very keen to see others concede.

challenges.name: The Pin
challenges.description: At one pub, sit so that a particular person can't leave their seat without asking you to move, and get them to ask at least once.
challenges.hint: At one stop, someone will sit awkwardly for their neighbour.

challenges.name: Threefold Repetition
challenges.description: Say the exact same sentence to the same person three different times without them commenting on it.
challenges.hint: Listen for something that sounds familiar... it may be because you've heard it before. Twice

challenges.name: The Queen
challenges.description: Get two different people to say "Oh no, my Queen!".
challenges.hint: Someone has their eye on royalty.

challenges.name: Skewer
challenges.description: Get two people to line up directly behind you, for example in a queue at the bar or walking single file between pubs. Do it three different times.
challenges.hint: Someone likes having company at their back.

challenges.name: Zwischenzug
challenges.description: Interrupt someone's story with a completely unrelated question, then let them carry on as if nothing happened. Do it three times.
challenges.hint: Someone's questions are... questionable.

challenges.name: I Adjust
challenges.description: Straighten or adjust one person's belongings (a glass, a phone, a coat) five times in the night without them commenting on it.
challenges.hint: One person's belongings are getting a lot of unasked-for attention.

challenges.name: Perpetual Check
challenges.description: Ask the same person "you alright?" or "you okay?" every time they come back to the table, all night.
challenges.hint: One person is receiving an unusual amount of concern.

decoys.name: The Watcher
decoys.description: Keep glancing at one particular person, as if you're tracking them for your challenge.

decoys.name: The Counter
decoys.description: Occasionally count something under your breath or on your fingers, then look satisfied.

decoys.name: The Interviewer
decoys.description: Ask people oddly specific questions, like their favourite vegetable or what their first phone was.

decoys.name: The Note-Taker
decoys.description: After certain conversations, type something into your phone notes slightly too visibly.

decoys.name: The Table Tapper
decoys.description: Tap the table once whenever you finish saying something. Looks a lot like hitting a chess clock.

decoys.name: The Word Lover
decoys.description: Pick an ordinary word like "interesting" or "fair enough" and use it noticeably often.

decoys.name: The Time Checker
decoys.description: Ask someone what time it is at every pub.

decoys.name: The Silent Celebrator
decoys.description: Do a tiny fist pump or smug smile after someone says something completely mundane.

decoys.name: The Toaster
decoys.description: Propose a toast at every pub, each one to something a bit more random than the last.

decoys.name: The Pointer
decoys.description: Point at things when you talk about them, even when there's no need to.

decoys.name: The Name Dropper
decoys.description: Mention the same famous chess player in conversation a few times.

decoys.name: The Handshaker
decoys.description: Shake hands with people when you arrive at each pub, as though it's important.

decoys.name: The Hummer
decoys.description: Hum the same short tune quietly a few times through the night.

decoys.name: The Agreer
decoys.description: Say "exactly" a bit too enthusiastically whenever someone makes a point.

decoys.name: The Hoverer
decoys.description: Hover your hand over something before picking up something else, all night.

decoys.name: The Long Thinker
decoys.description: Take an exaggerated pause before answering simple questions.

decoys.name: The Closer
decoys.description: Shake hands at the end of conversations rather than the start.

decoys.name: The Corner Cutter
decoys.description: Cross rooms diagonally whenever you can.

decoys.name: The Swapper
decoys.description: Quietly swap the positions of two items on the table.

decoys.name: The Planner
decoys.description: Keep asking people what they're doing next, after the crawl or this weekend.
